1 1.
In brief, the story of the prosecution is that on 27.06.2016, Ms. Pooja D/o Late Sh. Ram Gulam aged 14 years was reported to be missing and accordingly the FIR bearing no. 544/2016 was registered at PS Neb Sarai under Section 363 IPC.

On 29.06.2016, Ms. Pooja was traced and produced before CWC where she stated that she was placed at work at Saket H-Block and her employer's name is Ms.
Annu.
She also stated that she used to take care of two children Rachit, aged 10 years and Lalit, aged 2 years, her work hours were 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM and worked for approximately 3 months.
She stated that she worked for April, May and June and left her employment on 23.06.2024 and was paid Rs. 12,000/- for the entire period and was also provided food.
Upon directions of CWC, the present FIR bearing no. 591/2016 was registered at PS Neb Sarai against accused/ Annu Aggarwal.

She further stated before the SDM that during her employment, she had a peaceful time, she was not harassed in any manner, ,was provided food and was being kept with love and affection.
2.

Upon completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed u/s 173 Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C.') under Section 14 of Child and Adolescent Labour Act, 1986 was filed on 16.01.2017.
Cognizance was taken on the same day and a copy of the charge sheet was supplied to the accused in compliance with Section 207 Cr.P.C on 03.04.2017.

3. After considering the record and hearing the arguments, charge u/s 14 of Child and Adolescent Labour( Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (hereinafter referred as Child Labour Act) was framed against the accused Annu Aggarwal on 16.05.2017 to which the accused pleaded "not guilty"
and claimed trial.

After examination of above cited witnesses, PE was closed vide order dated 17.12.2020.
8.

To enable the accused to personally explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against him, the statement of the accused/ Annu Aggarwal, without oath, was recorded under Section 313 r/w 281 Cr.P.C on 02.04.2022.

In reply, the accused asserted her innocence and stated that she had employed only the mother of victim Pooja ie Ms. Guddi and Ms. Guddi brought her daughter/Pooja along with her for her safety as there used to be no one at the residence of Guddi and she could not leave her daughter/ Pooja alone.
Later, Pooja ran away with her boyfriend, and subsequently got married to him.
She has stated that she has been falsely implicated in the present case.
She chose to lead evidence in her defence.
9. Accused examined Mr. Arjun/ husband of Ms. Pooja in her defence.
DW-1/ Mr. Arjun stated that he has known Ms. Pooja since 2015.
At that time she was 14 years old.
He got married to Pooja in 2019.

10. Short point for determination before this court is as under:
"Whether- Ms. Pooja was under 14 years of age in April of 2016?
And if she was, was she being employed as a domestic worker by Ms. Annu Aggarwal/ accused during the period April to June 2016?"

Digitally signed by NIDHI NIDHI SINGH SINGH Date:
2024.02.28 17:30:38 +0530 11.

Ld. APP submitted that the case has been proved beyond reasonable doubt with the testimonies of all PWs and documents relied upon during evidence and has thus prayed that the accused be convicted of the offence charged u/s 14 Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986.
12. Per Contra, Ld. Counsel for the accused has submitted that the accused is completely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It has further been argued that firstly Ms. Pooja was never employed by the accused and that mother of the Ms. Pooja ie Ms. Guddi was employed by the accused and Ms. Pooja used to accompany her and there was no one at the house of Ms. Guddi to look after her when she was at work.

Further, age of Ms. Pooja being under 14 years in April 2016 has also not been established by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt as various contradictions have come to light by subjecting the witnesses to cross examination and that Ms. Pooja as well as her mother have admitted that she was over 14 years of age at the time of alleged employment in April 2016.
Further, husband of Ms. Pooja has also deposed in favor of the accused that Pooja was over 14 years of age in April 2016.

Ld. counsel finally submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and that, therefore, the benefit of the same ought to be extended to the accused, and that the accused is liable to be acquitted of the alleged offence.

3 13.
This Court has given thoughtful consideration to the material appearing on record as well as the arguments.
Before dwelling into the facts of the present case, it would be apt to discuss the legal standards required to be met by both sides.
In criminal law, the burden of proving the guilt of the accused exclusively lies on the prosecution which must prove the offences charged beyond reasonable doubt.
The benefit of doubt, if any, must go in favour of the accused.
Digitally signed by NIDHI NIDHI SINGH SINGH
Accused-
Annu Aggarwal has been charged with Section 14 of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986.

Same has been reproduced under for reference:
Section 14. Penalties.-
(1) Whoever employs any child or permits any child to work in contravention of the provisions of section 3 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than three months but which may extend to one year or with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but which may extend to twenty thousand rupees or with both.

(2) "Whoever, having been convicted of an offence under section 3, commits a like offence afterwards, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than six months but which may extend to two years.

(3) Whoever-(a) fails to give notice as required by section 9; or (b) fails to maintain a register as required by section 11 or makes any false entry in any such register; or (c) fails to display a notice containing an abstract of section 3 and this section as required by section 12; or (d) fails to comply with or contravenes any other provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder, shall be punishable with simple imprisonment which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.

15. It is also pertinent to make reference to Section 3 of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation)
Act, 1986 and Section 2 (ii) which defines child.

Prohibition of employment of children in certain occupations and processes- No child shall be employed or permitted to work in any of the occupations set forth in Part A of the Schedule or in any State vs Annu Aggarwal on 28 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76286395/
4 workshop wherein any of the processes set forth in Part B of the Schedule is carried on:
Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to any workshop wherein any process is carried on by the occupier with the aid of his family or to any school established by, or receiving assistance or recognition from, Government.
16.
The case of the prosecution, as sought to be established, falls within Part A of Schedule of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 at Point 14.

Same has been reproduced under for reference:
"....(14) Employment of children as domestic workers or servants;..."
17. Coming to the testimonies of prosecution witnesses, PW-1/Ms. Pooja herself has stated in her evidence recorded on 28.06.2017 that she is 17/18 years of age.
The alleged employment at the house of the accused is stated to have been done in April 2016 which makes her 16 years of age at the time of her employment.
The husband of Ms. Pooja ie Mr. Arjun/DW-1 has been examined in Court who has admitted that she was 15 years of age in the year 2016 and that he got married to her in the year 2019.
Further, mother of Ms. Pooja ie PW-2/ Ms. Guddi has also stated in her evidence recorded on 21.03.2018 that "...Today my daughter is 18 years of age...".
She has further stated in her evidence that she used to take her daughter along with her to play with the children.
She has further stated in her cross examination that at the time of death of her husband in 2009, her daughter was 8-10 years of age and that her son Deepak was 10-12 years of age.
Her husband was illiterate but only knew how to append his signatures.

She has further stated that she had gotten her daughter Ms. Pooja admitted in school and at the time of admission in school, Pooja's age was 7 NIDHI Digitally signed by NIDHI SINGH SINGH Date: 2024.02.28 17:30:54 +0530 years and that affidavit Ex. PW-4/B was prepared upon instructions from the teacher as Pooja was already 7 years of age and the criteria for admission to school was 5 years.
PW-4 has stated in his cross examination that Mr. Deepak, brother of Ms. Pooja, was 20 years old on 27.06.2016 and had lodged a missing complaint.
Prosecution has tried to establish the age of Ms. Pooja only through the school documents received from the concerned School.
No bone ossification test report is on record and there is no birth certificate also on record to prove the exact age of Ms. Pooja.

Further, PW-3/ Ms.
Reeta Singh, primary school teacher from SDMC Primary Girls School, Devli Village has reflected in her evidence that no birth documents such as birth certificate issued by MCD were seen at the time of admission in School.

sentences.text: Section 10 of the Child Labour Act states that if any question arises between an Inspector and an occupier as to the age of any child who is employed or is permitted to work by him in an establishment, the question shall, in the absence of a certificate as to the age of such child granted by the prescribed medical authority, be referred by the Inspector for decision to the prescribed medical authority.
In the present case, IO has not taken due steps to confirm the age of the victim from a medical authority.

18. In criminal jurisprudence, an accused is presumed to be innocent, until proven guilty, and the burden of proving the guilt of the accused solely rests upon the prosecution by leading positive evidence.
Accused is not expected to prove his innocence to the hilt.

If the prosecution appears to be State vs Annu Aggarwal on 28 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76286395/
5 improbable or lacks credibility the benefit of doubt necessarily has to go to the accused.
The guilt of the accused is not to be proved by mere preponderance of probabilities but it has to be proved beyond all reasonable doubts.

It is for the prosecution to travel the entire distance from "may have"
to "must have".
Suspicion, howsoever grave, cannot take the place of proof.
Digitally signed NIDHI bySINGH NIDHI SINGH Date: 2024.02.28 17:30:59 +0530 19.

Thus, in view of the foregoing analysis, this court is of the considered view that the aforesaid deficiencies in the case of the prosecution are sufficient to raise a doubt on the veracity of the entire prosecution case against the accused and the benefit of doubt is extended to her.

Prosecution has miserably failed in proving its case beyond reasonable doubt that Ms. Pooja was firstly under 14 years of age in April 2016 and that she was employed by the accused as a domestic worker.
Accordingly, accused Annu Aggarwal stands acquitted of the offence under Section 14 of Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 in the present case.
Announced in open Court on this 29th day of February 2024.
This Judgment consists of 9 pages and each page bears my signature.
